title: Authorization-evidence automation for SWFT, CSRMC, FedRAMP 20x and Zero Trust target-level (turning pipeline artifacts, SBOMs and control inheritance into AO-acceptable, reciprocally reusable packages)
problem: DoD programs, software factories and commercial ISVs still assemble authorization and zero-trust evidence by hand into eMASS/Xacta/spreadsheets while the target regimes (SWFT since May 2025, CSRMC since Sept 2025, FedRAMP 20x mandatory Jan 2027, ZT target level by 30 Sep 2027) all demand machine-readable, continuously refreshed, reciprocally reusable evidence - and no tool is yet proven to turn pipeline artifacts (SBOMs, scans, STIG/InSpec results, inherited controls, IdP/EDR telemetry) into packages a second authorizing official will accept without re-work.
echelons: DoD CIO / component CISO and AO staff

user.exact_role: ISSM/ISSO and Security Control Assessor (SCA) staff who build and validate the authorization package; software-factory compliance leads; program zero-trust leads reporting to the DoD CIO ZT PfMO; ISV compliance engineers preparing SWFT attestations, SBOMs and FedRAMP 20x KSI evidence
user.echelon: Program office / enterprise platform / supplier (not the warfighting chain)
organization_examples: Army PEO EIS and PEO C3N program ISSMs
Platform One / Kessel Run / cArmy software-factory compliance teams
DoD CIO Zero Trust Portfolio Management Office assessors
DISA and Fourth Estate AO staffs
Commercial SaaS/ISVs onboarding via Second Front Game Warden, UDS Army or Palantir FedStart
FedRAMP 20x applicants (cloud ISVs selling to DoD and civilian agencies)

current_workflow: 1. Engineers export scanner, STIG/CKL, InSpec, SBOM and signing outputs from the CI/CD pipeline (Big Bang, UDS, Game Warden, GitLab) as files.

2. Compliance staff map those artifacts to NIST SP 800-53 controls, ZT Overlay activities and (for suppliers) NIST SP 800-218/SWFT risk characteristics in spreadsheets or a GRC tool (eMASS, Xacta, RegScale).
3. Narratives (SSP, POA&M, control implementation statements) are written by hand or with generic LLM help and uploaded to eMASS; screenshots and logs from IdP/EDR/SIEM are attached as ZT evidence.
4. An SCA validates manually; the AO reviews PDFs and signs a 1-3 year ATO or a cATO with conditions.
5. A second component's AO usually re-reviews the package rather than accepting it (reciprocity fails); FedRAMP packages are re-expressed separately for 20x KSIs.
6. Re-assessment repeats annually, on major change, and again when the regime changes (cATO 2022 -> SWFT 2025 -> CSRMC 2025 -> ZT deadline 2027).
current_solution: eMASS (DISA) as system of record; Telos Xacta 360 and RegScale/Paramify-class GRC platforms (OSCAL-native); Vanta/Drata for FedRAMP-oriented ISVs; Ask Sage 'ATO In a Box' and similar LLM narrative generators; Anchore/Sonatype/Chainguard for SBOM generation and vulnerability evidence; MITRE SAF, Heimdall, Vulcan, compliance-trestle and GSA fedramp-automation as open-source utilities; Defense Unicorns UDS and Second Front Game Warden for inherited-control hosting; Booz Allen, GDIT, Deloitte and SecureStrux-type assessment services; NSA ZIG phase checklists for ZT.
failure: The tools produce data and documents, not acceptance: (a) the mapping layer between pipeline artifacts and the target regime is rebuilt by hand each time the regime changes, and the SWFT/CSRMC evidence formats are still not fully published; (b) reciprocity fails at the AO-to-AO handoff (DoD CIO's own 2025 study says AOs are 'biased to caution' and reciprocity guidance is unclear), so a machine-generated package is still re-adjudicated; (c) OSCAL, the intended interchange format, proved too heavy for most teams (Lula retired on that basis) while eMASS ingests OSCAL only in narrow demonstrations; (d) ZT activity status must be evidenced from heterogeneous IdP/EDR/SIEM telemetry that brownfield systems do not emit.

evidence.claim: DoD CIO 'Accelerating Secure Software' memo (24 Apr 2025) launched SWFT to replace point-in-time ATO/RMF for software with third-party assessment of vendor posture, third-party-certified SBOMs and AI-assisted back-end review; three RFIs were issued to industry.

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoD CIO published a combined summary of the three SWFT RFIs (Dec 2025) reporting 500+ industry responses; the tools RFI found companies concerned about inconsistent attestation requirements and that 'the amount of evidence required for NIST SP 800-218 compliance would likely require automation and integration of multiple tools within existing infrastructure'; a separate 'SWFT External Assessment Methodologies' RFI was posted on SAM.gov.

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons. (1) The paying customer and the accepting authority are different people: ISVs and program offices pay, but AOs decide, and AOs are 'biased to caution' and have no budget line for tools that make their job riskier-looking; a startup cannot sell acceptance, only artifacts. (2) The target moved three times in four years (cATO 2022, SWFT 2025, CSRMC 2025) and the SWFT/CSRMC evidence schemas are still being defined via RFIs, so any mapping engine built in 2024-2025 is partly obsolete and vendors have rationally stayed generic (OSCAL/800-53) rather than DoD-regime-specific. (3) The money went to inheritance hosts (Game Warden, UDS, FedStart, Platform One) that make the package problem disappear for tenants by absorbing it, and to GRC incumbents (Xacta has USAF-wide deployment via AWS; RegScale/Paramify/Vanta/Drata already hold FedRAMP 20x positions) who can add SBOM/AI features faster than a new entrant can win an AO's trust. What remains genuinely unsolved - a cross-regime, provenance-carrying evidence compiler that a second AO accepts - is blocked by policy (reciprocity practice) more than by technology.
technical_wedge: An 'evidence compiler' rather than another GRC dashboard: a signed, content-addressed evidence graph that ingests pipeline artifacts once (Syft/Grype/Trivy SBOM+vuln, cosign attestations, InSpec/CKL STIG results, Kubernetes policy state from UDS/Big Bang, IdP/EDR/SIEM control telemetry) and emits regime-specific views with full provenance: eMASS-importable 800-53 evidence, SWFT vendor attestation plus certified-SBOM diff (vendor SBOM vs third-party SBOM), CSRMC phase evidence, FedRAMP 20x KSI machine-readable package, and NSA ZIG activity status. The defensible piece is the crosswalk plus the 'AO acceptance record': logging which evidence forms which AO accepted, so packages can be re-presented to a second AO with a precedent trail. Sell first to ISVs already on an accredited host (they have budget, urgency from SWFT Phase 2 third-party assessment and FedRAMP 20x, and need no SBIR eligibility), then to software factories. Do not build a hosting platform, a scanner or an LLM narrative generator - all three are crowded.

mvp.what: CLI plus small web review app: takes SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX), Grype/Trivy scan JSON, InSpec/CKL results and cosign attestations from a UDS or Big Bang pipeline; produces (a) an eMASS-importable control-evidence bundle, (b) a SWFT-style attestation with vendor-vs-assessor SBOM diff, and (c) a FedRAMP 20x KSI evidence JSON, each item carrying a provenance link back to the originating artifact hash; includes a reviewer workflow that records accept/reject per evidence item.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for a strong engineer: all inputs are open formats with open tooling; a reference pipeline can be built on UDS Core / Big Bang open source and public FedRAMP 20x KSI definitions; demo target is an unclassified ISV app on a commercial Kubernetes cluster.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That one SCA/ISSM at a software factory or one 3PAO/assessor accepts the generated bundle with materially less re-work than today (measured hours), and that at least one evidence item is reused across two regimes without re-collection. If no assessor will review it, the gap is not real for a startup.

data_requirement.what: Pipeline artifacts (SBOMs, scan results, STIG/InSpec results, signatures), control catalogs and crosswalks (NIST SP 800-53 r5, 800-171, 800-218/SSDF, FedRAMP 20x KSIs, DoD ZT Overlays, NSA ZIG activity lists, SWFT 12 risk characteristics once published), sample accepted packages and AO feedback for calibration.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Artifacts and catalogs: yes, all open or generated from open-source apps. SWFT/CSRMC schemas: partially - only what DoD CIO publishes. Real DoD system packages are CUI and generally unobtainable pre-contract; ISV-side packages are obtainable under NDA from pilot customers. Accepted-package exemplars are the scarce asset.

budget.program_or_line: No dedicated appropriation found. Government demand is funded from component IT/cyber O&M lines, software-factory budgets and SBIR (AF254-D0802 D2P2, FY25). ISV demand is funded from vendors' own compliance/GTM budgets (FedRAMP 20x and SWFT third-party assessment costs).
budget.evidence: AF SBIR D2P2 topic AF254-D0802 (open 7 May - 25 Jun 2025) targets RMF automation with Phase III cATO+ConMon; GAO-25-107649 shows $10.9B (FY23-25) across 24 IT programs that must plan ZT by 2027; DoD CIO SWFT and CSRMC budgets: Public evidence insufficient. IDIQ ceilings for hosting/cloud (JWCC, Cloud One) are not revenue for this gap.

entry_vehicle.primary: Commercial SaaS sale to ISVs already hosted on an accredited platform (Game Warden, UDS Army, FedStart) or preparing FedRAMP 20x - no SBIR eligibility test, real budgets, dated deadlines (SWFT third-party assessment phase, 20x Jan 2027).
sequence: 1. Build open-source core (evidence graph + crosswalks) to earn software-factory and 3PAO trust; publish FedRAMP 20x KSI and SWFT crosswalks.
2. Pilot with 2-3 hosted ISVs and one 3PAO/assessor; measure re-work hours saved and record first assessor acceptance.
3. Partner with a hosting platform (Game Warden/UDS) or GRC incumbent as a plug-in rather than compete.

4. If cap table permits, AFWERX D2P2 / open-topic SBIR for the government-side (eMASS/ZT) connectors; otherwise subcontract to an assessment integrator (Booz Allen, GDIT, SecureStrux-type) on a program ZT assessment.
5. Pursue Tradewinds/CSO or a software-factory task order for a program-office deployment once one AO has accepted packages.
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% U.S. ownership and control by U.S. citizens or permanent residents; with one German founder expected to become a permanent resident and one Indonesian founder who is not a U.S. person, the cap table would need U.S.-person majority (e.g., U.S. co-founder/investors) - counsel required. The commercial-ISV entry path avoids this. Handling DoD-system CUI (SSPs, vulnerability data) triggers DFARS 252.204-7012 / NIST SP 800-171 and, for export-controlled CUI, ITAR/EAR access questions for the non-U.S.-person founder; ISV-side SBOM and commercial pipeline data is generally not controlled. No clearance needed for the MVP; program deployments at IL5+ and any classified enclave work would require cleared U.S.-person staff.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily, but the relevant incumbents are not the C4ISR primes - they are Telos, RegScale, Paramify, Vanta/Drata, Ask Sage, and the hosting platforms (Second Front, Defense Unicorns, Palantir FedStart). Palantir already sells FedStart inheritance; Defense Unicorns has open-source compliance tooling history (Lula) and $136M of new capital; Xacta already ingests scanner output. Any of them can ship a SWFT/CSRMC/20x crosswalk in one or two quarters once DoD CIO publishes schemas. The government itself may furnish SWFT back-end tooling, which would collapse the government-side market.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: A startup wins only if it (a) owns the cross-regime evidence graph with provenance as open infrastructure that hosts and GRC tools embed rather than rebuild, and (b) accumulates the first AO/3PAO acceptance precedents before incumbents bother. That is plausible as a niche, cash-flowing business selling to ISVs (dual-use with FedRAMP 20x), but the moat is thin and the ceiling is a GRC feature, not a platform. Honest verdict: viable as a focused compliance-automation company or as an acquisition target for a host/GRC vendor; weak as a venture-scale C4ISR thesis.

capital_required.assumptions: PoC: two founders plus one contractor for 6 months on open-source pipelines, no accreditation. Credible demo: pilot with 2-3 hosted ISVs and one assessor, a part-time former SCA/ISSM adviser, IL4 hosting via a partner platform (tenant fees), 12-18 months. First production: obtaining an own FedRAMP 20x Low/Moderate or IL4 authorization for the SaaS (or riding a host), eMASS API integration, a cleared U.S.-person compliance lead, sales cycle of 9-18 months into a software factory or program office; excludes any classified-enclave variant. All figures are analyst estimates (INFERENCE, LOW confidence).

expertise_required.role: Former DoD SCA / ISSM or AO-staff practitioner (ideally from a software factory or component CISO office)
expertise_required.why: Knows what an AO actually accepts, how eMASS is used in practice, and who to call; without this the product is a data tool with no acceptance path.

expertise_required.role: Supply-chain/DevSecOps engineer fluent in SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX), in-toto/SLSA attestations, cosign, Kubernetes policy and OSCAL
expertise_required.why: Builds the evidence graph and pipeline connectors; the strong engineer founder can cover this.
Needed to make the ISV-side output assessor-acceptable and to sell the dual-use path.
SBIR eligibility with non-U.S.-person founder, CUI handling under DFARS 7012, and any ITAR/EAR exposure when handling program data.

expertise_required.role: Federal sales lead with GRC/host partnerships
expertise_required.why: Distribution through Game Warden/UDS/GRC vendors matters more than direct government sales.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The MVP is unclassified commercial software on open formats. Burden rises when the product touches real DoD system packages (CUI: DFARS 252.204-7012, NIST SP 800-171, possibly CMMC Level 2 for the company), when it is hosted as SaaS for DoD users (IL4/IL5 or FedRAMP 20x authorization for the product itself - the same burden it helps others with), and when eMASS API access is needed (DISA-gated). No ITAR is inherent to the software, but program data it processes may be export-controlled.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person founder can build and sell the ISV-facing product. Access to DoD CUI (SSPs, vulnerability findings of DoD systems) is governed by contract clauses and, where the CUI is export-controlled, by ITAR/EAR deemed-export rules; this needs counsel and likely role separation (the non-U.S.-person founder stays off government-CUI environments). Any IL5/classified deployment work requires U.S.-person, cleared staff. SBIR/STTR needs a U.S.-person-majority cap table. These are constraints to design around, not definitive legal judgments.

dual_use_potential.explanation: FedRAMP 20x (all federal cloud vendors), StateRAMP/GovRAMP, CMMC and SSDF attestations use the same pipeline-artifact-to-evidence problem; the ISV market is commercial and larger than the DoD program market. The DoD-specific crosswalks (SWFT, CSRMC, ZT overlays, eMASS) are the differentiator but not the only market.

defensibility.explanation: Proprietary value would be the maintained crosswalks between regimes, the connectors into gated interfaces (eMASS API, hosts' pipelines), the product's own authorization, and above all the accumulated record of which evidence forms were accepted by which AOs/assessors (precedent data). Algorithms are not defensible (mapping and LLM summarization are commodity); network effects are weak unless AOs adopt the acceptance record as a shared reciprocity ledger - which would need DoD CIO sponsorship.

why_now: In ~18 months the rules changed from narrative-based, point-in-time authorization to evidence-based continuous authorization on three fronts at once: SWFT (Apr/May 2025, 500+ RFI responses, moving from pilot to requirement in 2026 with third-party SBOM certification), CSRMC (Sep 2025, automation and reciprocity as tenets), FedRAMP 20x (2026 rules mandatory 1 Jan 2027, Rev5 intake ends 11 Jun 2027) and the ZT target-level deadline (30 Sep 2027) with NSA's Jan 2026 ZIGs enumerating the activities. The Jan 2026 AI strategy names ATO blockers explicitly. Meanwhile, SBOM/attestation tooling (Syft, cosign, SLSA, CycloneDX 1.6) and LLM summarization became commodity, so the evidence-generation side is cheap; the unsolved part is acceptance and reuse.
killer_risk: The acceptance problem is a policy and incentive problem the startup cannot fix: AOs remain 'biased to caution', reciprocity is unenforced, and DoD CIO may furnish or mandate its own SWFT/CSRMC tooling (or anoint Xacta/RegScale-class incumbents), leaving a startup with a commodity artifact converter in a crowded GRC market where Paramify, Vanta, Drata, RegScale and Telos already hold FedRAMP 20x/DoD positions and hosts like Game Warden/UDS make the problem disappear for exactly the ISVs the startup would target. Low willingness to pay for software versus services (S10) compounds this.

allied_extension: Moderately more compelling. The same evidence-once-reuse-many problem exists for UK (Secure by Design / Cyber Essentials Plus), Germany (BSI C5, which Game Warden already lists), NATO (NIAS/NCIA accreditation) and Australia (IRAP), and ISVs selling to several allied governments must re-express the same pipeline evidence per regime - a natural extension of the crosswalk engine. A German founder helps with BSI C5/EU markets. Counter: allied accreditation authorities are even more manual and relationship-driven than DoD AOs, crosswalks between national schemes are not officially recognized, and the startup would need in-country presence and counsel for each. Allied value is real for the ISV-facing product, weak for the DoD-program-facing product.
